title: South Korea's LoL National Team Sweeps Team USA 3-0 in Under an Hour
summary: South Korea's LoL National Team Sweeps Team USA 3-0 in Under an Hour  invenglobal.com
content:
The South Korean LoL national team for the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games secured a dominant 3-0 victory against Team USA on Day 1 of the 'LoL National Team Evaluation Matches' held at the Busan Cinema Center on September 19. They closed out Game 1 in 20 minutes, Game 2 in 19 minutes, and Game 3 in the 20-minute mark.

South Korea was overwhelming right from Game 1. Kim 'Zeka' Geon-woo's Ryze secured a solo kill against 'Aojune''s Anivia right at the start, and soon after, Kim 'Canyon' Geon-bu's Qiyana ganked top lane to score a solo kill on opposing top laner 'Denathor'. Qiyana also dropped by mid lane, where Ryze held firm lane priority, to claim an extra kill.

While 'Scary Jerry' and 'Zyko', who were anchoring Team USA's bottom lane, put up a fight, South Korea's hyper-scaled topside outperformed them in every aspect—from skirmishes to macro play—widening the gap rapidly. Qiyana eventually became Legendary, leading the team in damage dealt and driving the victory in Game 1.

Game 2 also started with early impact from 'Canyon''s Pantheon. After stealing the opponent's Gromp, Pantheon rotated to a bottom lane where trades had gone favorably, cleanly picking up a double kill. Lee 'Gumayusi' Min-hyeong's Caitlyn and Ryu 'Keria' Min-seok's Bard also turned the tables on opposing jungler 'Perry''s Jarvan IV during a gank, while Pantheon visited bot lane once again to pick up two more kills.

With Bard untethered to his lane, he roamed all over the map, exerting a presence like a second jungler. The global gold gap widened rapidly. A flank Teleport targeting Caitlyn was thwarted by a clutch save from a well-timed Bard. Expanding their lead to a 10,000 gold difference by the 12-minute mark, the South Korean team took Game 2 with a dominant kill score of 34-5.

In Game 3, Team USA finally managed to score some early points. In a 2v2 top-jungle skirmish, 'Denathor''s Gnar secured a double kill. However, having already suffered losses during the early invade skirmish, Team USA's bot side continued to bleed out, and once 'Zeka''s Twisted Fate and 'Zeus''s Shen stepped in to help, the balance completely collapsed.

title: David vs. Goliath: Maryville Esports Takes on Korea’s Greatest Team Ever Assembled
summary: David vs. Goliath: Maryville Esports Takes on Korea’s Greatest Team Ever Assembled  Maryville University
content:
Threeindividualswill step onto one of the biggest stages in the history of competitive gaming. On Saturday, September 19, JunHao“AoJune“Chen, Jeremiah “ScaryJerry“Leathe, and Ryan “Zyko” Jung will wear the red, white, and blue in an internationalLeague of Legends(LoL)showdown against South Korea’s national teaminafriendly.

This isn’t just any roster; it’s a Maryville reunion on the international stage:

2,500 fans packed into the stunning Busan Cinema Center, the electric atmosphere of a Korean esports crowd, and a broadcast beamed exclusively on Disney+ across North America, Europe, and Southeast Asia. The match will be hosted by the Korea e-Sports Association (KeSPA), which invited the United States as one of just two international opponents alongside Vietnam to sharpen its squad for the Asian Games. KeSPA is rolling out the red carpet, covering housing, meals, ground transportation, and practice facilities for the entire delegation.

This tier-two, semi-pro roster was assembled by Nick “Inero” Smith, head coach of the USA Esports LoL program and a veteran of the North American professional scene. He’ll be joined on the bench by Aiden “Niles” Tidwell, Maryville’s head LoL coach, traveling with the delegation to assist the coaching staff. Dan Clerke, national team manager for USA Esports, andMaryville University’s director of esports,is coordinating the entire operation. While North America’s top league sits in the middle of its playoffs and couldn’t release its players, the door swung open and Maryville’s finest walked through.

“Being a part of this means the world to me,” said Aiden Tidwell. “I love my country, so having the chance torepresentthem is something I will always cherish. Also, playing against some of the greatest players of all time makes this a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity —we’llmake the most of this trip.”
